la:noun:adytum.html:
ădўtum, i, n., = ἄδυτον (not to be entered),
the innermost part of a temple, the sanctuary, which none but priests could enter, and from which oracles were delivered.
Lit.: in occultis ac remotis templi, quae Graeci ἄδυτα appellant, : aeternumque adytis effert penetralibus ignem,: isque adytis haec tristia dicta reportat,; 6, 98; .—In gen., a secret place, chamber; of the dead, a grave, tomb, in , and : descriptionem cubiculorum in adytis, chambers in secret places, i. e. inner chambers, .—
Fig.: ex adyto tamquam cordis responsa dedere, the inmost recesses, * .!*? In Attius also masc. adўtus, ūs: adytus augura, in (Trag. Rel. p. 217 Rib.).
